orders.reason: Follow-up of right lower lobe pneumonia

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 10 days after admission for RLL pneumonia, discharged 12/24. Discharge summary reviewed: ceftriaxone/azithro inpatient, no antibiotics at discharge. A glucose drop from 228 to 112 after the hospital's morning glargine was noted, no symptoms, attributed to the insulin.

Now: cough much better, a little sputum in the mornings, no fever. Energy coming back. Home sugars 120s-160s on his usual bedtime glargine, no lows. Med list reconciled against the discharge list, no changes. Smoked a few cigarettes since getting home; we talked about it.

Exam: afebrile, sat normal on room air. Few crackles R base, otherwise clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P: CAP, resolving. CBC and BMP today. Follow-up 2-view CXR mid-February. Smoking - strongly advised to use this as the moment to quit; he'll think about it. Nephrology visit later this month.

Mr. Dabrowski came in on 1/17/2018, recovering from his December pneumonia. Kidney function back at his baseline after the admission, CKD stage 4. PTH is up again, 412, calcium normal. Continue calcitriol and sevelamer as they are, and we will repeat calcium, phosphorus and PTH at a 6-month visit.

Medications unchanged. NKDA.

Nephrology

events.reason: CKD follow-up, weakness and bone pain

documents.title: Nephrology consultation letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Dabrowski on 6/22/2018 for his scheduled CKD visit, his first since January. For the last few months he has felt generally weak and has had aching in his bones. No falls or injuries.

BP 145/90. On exam there is a firm, non-tender mass low in the neck, which I could not feel at earlier visits.

Labs today: calcium 11.2 mg/dL, phosphorus 5.8 mg/dL, creatinine 3.4 mg/dL (eGFR about 19), PTH 800 pg/mL.

Impression: hypercalcemia with markedly elevated PTH after years of secondary hyperparathyroidism of CKD: tertiary hyperparathyroidism, with a palpable gland likely.

Plan: neck ultrasound; referral to endocrine surgery for evaluation for parathyroidectomy. Continue sevelamer. We will keep calcitriol at the current dose until surgery is decided. He should keep up fluids.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, sevelamer carbonate 800 mg three times daily with meals, calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Nephrology

documents.title: Call re: parathyroid
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after reading the nephrology letter. Explained the parathyroid glands are overactive and pushing his calcium up, likely why he aches. He has the ultrasound booked for next week and is waiting to hear from the surgeons. Moved his July visit up so we can go over it.

reports.text: Ultrasound of the neck. Thyroid gland normal in size and echotexture, no thyroid nodules. Posterior to the lower pole of the right thyroid lobe is a well-defined hypoechoic oval structure measuring 2.4 cm, consistent with an enlarged parathyroid gland. A second hypoechoic structure posterior to the lower pole of the left lobe measures 1.1 cm, also consistent with parathyroid tissue. No cervical lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged right inferior parathyroid gland 2.4 cm and left inferior parathyroid 1.1 cm. Normal thyroid.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the parathyroid news. Still achy in the hips, shins and back, tired by midafternoon. No kidney stones that he knows of. No falls.

Ultrasound 7/5: enlarged R inferior parathyroid 2.4 cm and a smaller L inferior gland; thyroid normal. Endocrine surgery consult set for August.

Exam: neck - firm nodule low R side, non-tender. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Tertiary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia - surgery consult pending. Fluids, avoid calcium supplements.
2. DM2 - A1c, UACR, lipids today.
3. Bone pain - acetaminophen as before. Reminded him: no ibuprofen or naproxen with his kidneys.
4. CKD 4, HTN, CAD - unchanged.

documents.title: Endocrine surgery consultation
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for sharing the care of Mr. Dabrowski, seen 8/9/2018 at the request of his nephrologist. He has stage 4 CKD from diabetes with years of secondary hyperparathyroidism, now with calcium 11.2, phosphorus 5.8 and PTH 800, and several months of weakness and bone aching.

Exam: palpable right inferior neck nodule, non-tender. Vocal quality normal.

Imaging: ultrasound shows a 2.4 cm right inferior gland and a 1.1 cm left inferior gland. Sestamibi scan done here shows uptake in more than one gland, strongest at the right inferior position.

Assessment: tertiary hyperparathyroidism with multigland disease.

Recommendation: subtotal parathyroidectomy with bilateral neck exploration, leaving a remnant of the most normal-appearing gland. Risks reviewed including hoarseness, low calcium afterward and persistence or recurrence. He would like to go ahead; surgery scheduled 9/12. Aspirin may continue.

Endocrine Surgery

reports.text: Specimens: right inferior parathyroid, right superior parathyroid, left inferior parathyroid, and a portion of the left superior parathyroid. Gross: four pieces of tan-brown soft tissue, the largest 2.4 cm (right inferior). Microscopic: hypercellular parathyroid tissue with chief cell hyperplasia and reduced stromal fat in each specimen. No atypia. Frozen sections confirmed parathyroid tissue.
reports.conclusion: Parathyroid hyperplasia, multiple glands, consistent with tertiary hyperparathyroidism. No malignancy.

documents.title: Operative and discharge note
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
Procedure 9/12/2018: bilateral neck exploration with subtotal parathyroidectomy. All four glands identified and enlarged. Right inferior, right superior and left inferior glands removed; about half of the left superior gland left in place with its blood supply and marked with a clip. Intraoperative PTH fell appropriately. Recurrent laryngeal nerves seen and preserved. Estimated blood loss minimal.

Overnight observation. Voice normal. Morning PTH 48 pg/mL, calcium 8.7 mg/dL without tingling or cramping. Discharged 9/13 on his usual medications including calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily; nephrology to adjust. Watch for numbness around the mouth or hand cramps.

Pathology: multigland parathyroid hyperplasia, benign.

Follow-up: surgical clinic in 2 weeks; calcium with his PCP in about 10 days.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-op follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from subtotal parathyroidectomy. Neck sore for a few days, now fine. No tingling, no cramps. Voice normal. Says the bone aching is already a little better.

Op note and path reviewed: multigland hyperplasia, benign; remnant of L superior left in place.

Exam: incision clean and healing, no swelling. Chvostek negative.

A/P: s/p subtotal parathyroidectomy for tertiary HPT - calcium today; resolve from active list. Calcitriol per nephrology. Flu shot next month at nurse visit.

documents.title: Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Several months of feeling worn out, can't finish the leaf raking he used to do in an afternoon. Gets lightheaded standing up sometimes. No chest pain, no black or bloody stools, no bleeding anywhere. Appetite a bit off.

On review of what he takes at home: he's been using over-the-counter ibuprofen, 2 tabs a few times a week, since the summer for knees and the bone aching. Didn't think of it as a medicine.

Exam: pale. BP per flowsheet, no orthostatic drop on standing. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema.

Labs today: Hgb 9.5, down from his usual low 11s-12. Creatinine 3.8, higher than his baseline around 3.

A/P
1. Anemia, worse - likely kidney related but he's due a proper workup; referred to hematology. Copy to nephrology.
2. CKD 4 with higher creatinine on NSAIDs - stop all ibuprofen. Acetaminophen only. Repeat with hematology labs.
3. Fatigue - as above.

documents.title: Hematology consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Dabrowski, 66, on 12/24/2018. He has diabetic nephropathy with CKD stage 4 and had a subtotal parathyroidectomy in September for tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

For a few months he has had low energy, tires quickly with activity and is occasionally dizzy. His appetite is down and food tastes metallic to him. He stopped over-the-counter NSAIDs last month because of his kidney numbers. No bleeding. He continues to smoke and drinks socially.

Exam: conjunctival pallor. Vibration sense reduced at both feet. No lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly.

Results: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, MCV 89 fL, reticulocyte count 0.4%, creatinine 3.9 mg/dL (eGFR about 16). Ferritin, transferrin saturation, TSH, B12 and folate are within normal limits. Stool guaiac negative. Peripheral smear: normocytic, normochromic red cells without abnormal forms; white cells and platelets unremarkable.

Impression: hypoproliferative normocytic anemia with replete iron and no evidence of bleeding, hemolysis or a marrow process: anemia of chronic kidney disease.

Recommendation: an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent is reasonable once his kidney function settles off NSAIDs; I have shared this with his nephrologist, who will decide timing and dosing. No further hematology follow-up needed unless the picture changes.

Medications reviewed: insulin glargine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, sevelamer, calcitriol, aspirin, acetaminophen. NKDA.

Hematology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hematology letter reviewed: anemia of CKD, iron/B12/folate/TSH normal, stool negative, smear unremarkable. They have handed the ESA question to nephrology.

Still tired. Off ibuprofen since November. No bleeding.

Feet: he says they feel 'like they're asleep' at the bottoms, mostly at night. Exam today: monofilament reduced at 4 of 10 sites on each foot, vibration reduced at both great toes, ankle jerks diminished. Skin intact, no calluses. DP faint but present.

A/P
1. Anemia of CKD - added to list. Nephrology to consider ESA.
2. Diabetic polyneuropathy - new on exam, foot care reviewed: daily foot checks, no barefoot walking, properly fitting shoes.
3. DM2 - A1c today.
4. CKD 4 - off NSAIDs, nephrology in March.

documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Seen 3/12/2019. Six months after subtotal parathyroidectomy, calcium is normal and PTH has come down to a range appropriate for stage 4 CKD. Creatinine has improved from 3.9 in December to the low 3s off ibuprofen. Hemoglobin remains in the mid 9s. I discussed the hematology recommendation with him; he would like to hold off on injections for now and recheck. We will revisit at the next visit.

Medications unchanged, including calcitriol 0.25 mcg daily and sevelamer with meals.

Nephrology

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Lives alone, independent in ADLs and IADLs, still drives. Daughter checks on him weekly. No falls, though he's more careful on stairs since the feet went numb. PHQ-2 1 (a few days of low energy, not low mood). Health care proxy form: daughter, signed copy scanned today.

Preventive: flu today (high-dose). Lung CT ordered for November. Eye exam August, no retinopathy. Shingles series done 2018. PPSV23 2015, PCV13 2017. Colonoscopy due 2024.

Counseling: tobacco - still smoking, offered varenicline vs patch, declined both for now. Alcohol 1-2 per week.

Next chronic disease visit in December.

reports.text: Annual low-dose CT chest. Comparison 11/06/2018. No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. No effusion or adenopathy.

documents.title: Still tired
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, I'm still dragging most days. Is this the blood count thing? My kidney appointment isn't until January 7. Should I come in sooner?

documents.title: RE: Still tired
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stan, it very likely is the anemia from your kidneys. Nephrology planned to talk about the injections that raise the blood count at that January visit, and it's worth having that conversation then. If you get chest pain, short of breath, black stools or feel faint, call us the same day and we'll see you. Otherwise keep the 1/7 appointment and I'll look for their letter.

Follow-up after his portal message. Tired but no chest pain, no dyspnea beyond baseline, no bleeding. Lung CT November clear.

Exam: pale conjunctivae. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet without lesions.

Plan: A1c today. Nephrology 1/7 for anemia treatment decision. Glargine and other meds unchanged.
